templates.pattern: [P1] starts from point A, walks [D1] km towards North, then turns right and walks [D2] km. Which direction is [P1] now facing?
templates.explanation: Started facing North. Turned right = now facing East.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks [D1] km East, then turns left and walks [D2] km. Which direction is [P1] facing now?
templates.explanation: Walking East then turning left = facing North.

templates.pattern: [P1] starts facing South. Turns right twice. Which direction is [P1] now facing?
templates.explanation: South → turn right → West → turn right → North.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks [D1] km North, then [D2] km South. How far is [P1] from the starting point and in which direction?
templates.explanation: [P1] walked [D1] km North and [D2] km South. Net = [D1]-[D2] km North.

templates.pattern: [P1] faces North. Turns right, then turns right again, then turns left. Which direction is [P1] now facing?
templates.explanation: North → right → East → right → South → left → East.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks [D1] km East, then [D2] km West. How far and in which direction is [P1] from start?
templates.explanation: Net displacement = [D1]-[D2] km East.

templates.pattern: [P1] starts from home, walks [D1] km North to market, then [D2] km East to school. How far is the school from home (straight line distance)?
templates.explanation: Right angle triangle: √([D1]²+[D2]²) = √([D1*D1]+[D2*D2]) km

templates.pattern: [P1] is facing West. Turns 180 degrees. Which direction is [P1] now facing?
templates.explanation: 180 degree turn reverses direction. West → East.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks [D1] km South, then turns left and walks [D2] km. Which direction is [P1] facing?
templates.explanation: Walking South then turning left = facing East.

templates.pattern: The sun rises in the East. [P1] stands so that the sun is on his right. Which direction is [P1] facing?
templates.explanation: Sun is in East = on right side. If East is to the right, [P1] is facing South.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks [D1] km North, then turns right and walks [D2] km, then turns right again and walks [D1] km. How far is [P1] from start and in which direction?
templates.explanation: North [D1] → East [D2] → South [D1]. North and South cancel. [P1] is [D2] km East of start.

templates.pattern: [P1] starts facing East. Makes a 90-degree turn to the left, then another 90-degree turn to the left. Which direction is [P1] now facing?
templates.explanation: East → left (North) → left (West).

templates.pattern: [P1] and [P2] start from the same point. [P1] walks [D1] km North and [P2] walks [D1] km South. How far apart are they?
templates.explanation: They walk in opposite directions. Total distance apart = [D1]+[D1] = 2×[D1].

templates.pattern: At 6 AM, [P1] stands facing the rising sun. After walking some distance, [P1] turns left. Which direction is [P1] now moving?
templates.explanation: Sun rises in East. Facing East. Turn left = now facing North.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks [D1] km to the North-East. If [P1] had walked only North, how far North would [P1] have reached? (Assume 45-degree angle, so North component = [D1]/√2 ≈ [D1]×0.7)
templates.explanation: North-East at 45° means equal North and East components. North component = [D1]/√2 ≈ [D1]×0.707

templates.pattern: [P1] is standing at point X facing North. [P2] is standing behind [P1]. Which direction is [P2] facing if [P2] faces [P1]?
templates.explanation: [P1] faces North. [P2] is behind [P1] = South of [P1]. To face [P1], [P2] must face North.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks [D1] km West, then turns right and walks [D2] km. Which direction is [P1] now facing?
templates.explanation: Walking West then turning right = now facing North.

templates.pattern: [P1] starts from point A, walks [D1] km North to B, then [D2] km East to C, then [D1] km South to D. What is the distance and direction of D from A?
templates.explanation: North [D1] + South [D1] cancel out. D is [D2] km East of A.

templates.pattern: If South-East is exactly between South and East, in which direction would [P1] be walking if [P1] is walking in the exact opposite direction of North-West?
templates.explanation: Opposite of North-West is South-East.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks [D1] km East, then turns North and walks [D2] km. What is the shortest distance from the starting point?
templates.explanation: Right angle triangle: √([D1]²+[D2]²) = [D1*D1+D2*D2] → √[answer] km

templates.pattern: [P1] faces South. Turns 90 degrees clockwise. Which direction does [P1] face?
templates.explanation: South + 90 degrees clockwise = West.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks [D1] km North, [D2] km East, [D1] km South, [D2] km West. Where is [P1] now relative to start?
templates.explanation: N[D1]+S[D1] cancel. E[D2]+W[D2] cancel. [P1] is back at the starting point.

templates.pattern: At sunset, [P1] stands with the sun directly behind. Which direction is [P1] facing?
templates.explanation: Sun sets in West. Sun is behind = West is behind. [P1] is facing East.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks [D1] km North, then turns left and walks [D2] km, then turns left again and walks [D3] km. How far is [P1] from start (North-South only)?
templates.explanation: North [D1] → left = West [D2] → left = South [D3]. Net North = [D1]-[D3].

templates.pattern: [P1] is [D1] km to the East of [P2]. [P3] is [D2] km to the North of [P2]. How far is [P1] from [P3]?
templates.explanation: Right angle triangle with legs [D1] and [D2]. Distance = √([D1]²+[D2]²)
